keySentence: Anne was very different from what they expected.

facts.Page story text 1 (draft, teacher check: Anne named everything she saw. She called a lake 'the Lake of Shining Waters.' Anne saw beauty everywhere. Anne was very different from what they expected.
facts.Page story text 2 (draft, teacher check: On the way to Green Gables, Anne talked nonstop with excitement. She gave beautiful names to every tree, road, and lake she saw. She called one lake 'the Lake of Shining Waters' because it sparkled. Matthew listened quietly and found himself charmed by this unusual girl. Anne was very different from what they expected. Anne had the special gift of seeing magic in ordinary things.
facts.Page story text 3 (draft, teacher check: During the carriage ride to Green Gables, Anne's mouth never stopped for a single moment. She gazed at the landscape with wonder-filled eyes and gave poetic names to everything she saw. A simple avenue of apple trees became 'the White Way of Delight' in her vivid imagination. Even quiet, shy Matthew found himself smiling at this extraordinary girl's endless enthusiasm. Anne was very different from what they expected. However, Marilla was less enchanted and worried that Anne was too dreamy and impractical. Because Anne saw the world differently from everyone else, not everyone understood or appreciated her at first. Yet it was this very ability to find beauty in the mundane that made Anne truly remarkable and irreplaceable.
